title: Protocol for detecting chromatin dynamics and screening chromatin relaxer by FRAP assay
protocol: Collect virus coding H1-GFP and HP1α-cherry.
Seed Plate-E cells in a 10 cm dish at about 50% confluence the day before transfection.
Transfect the cells with 10 μg plasmid encoding H1-GFP or HP1α-cherry, mixing with 40 μL PEI (1 mg/mL) per dish.
Collect the culture medium containing virus 48 hours after transfection and remove cell fragments with a 0.45 μm sterile filter.
Repeat the virus collection once 24 hours later after replacing fresh medium.
Store collected virus in 4°C for about 1 week or at -80°C for up to 1 year.
Seed model cells (MEF cells) on a 6 cm cell culture dish.
Add polybrene (6 ng/μL in final concentration) to the virus medium to improve infection efficiency.
Label MEF cells by adding 5 mL virus medium containing retrovirus coding for H1-GFP and HP1α-Cherry.
Use 4 mL of H1-GFP and 1 mL of HP1α-Cherry virus medium.
Repeat the infection step with 4 mL fresh virus medium containing only H1-GFP, 24 hours after the first infection.
Replace culture medium with fresh medium 12 hours after the secondary infection.
Check transfection efficiency with a fluorescence microscope 48–60 hours after the first infection.
Seed MEF cells in a 6-well dish after labeling them with H1-GFP and HP1α-Cherry.
Infect model cells with virus encoding test gene 12 hours after seeding the model cells.
Repeat the infection step once more to improve efficiency, 24 hours after the first infection.
Seed MEF cells on a confocal dish with glass bottom precoated with 0.1% gelatin or Poly-D-Lysine for attachment.
Culture the seeded cells in normal conditions at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 24-48 hours before imaging.
Place the dish on the stage of a microscope equipped with an incubator system for FRAP imaging.
Set up the confocal microscope for imaging and FRAP analysis.
Put the dish on the stage of the confocal microscope.
Prewarm the dish for 5-10 minutes.
Select a high magnification lens, such as 63× or 100× oil objective with N.A. ≥ 1.4.
Find and adjust the focus using the confocal microscope settings.
Set the frame size to no more than 512×512 pixels for improved acquiring rate.
Ensure that the acquisition time is less than 1 second per frame in single-channel mode.
Open the software of Zen 3 black edition.
Click the acquisition button and choose "Time series", "Bleaching", and "Regions".
Set the argon laser (or 488 nm laser) and 561 nm laser on.
Setup two trackers, one for EGFP and another for mCherry with proper filters.
Adjust the laser power and gain value for optimal imaging.
Set the zoom factor as 3 for a 63× objective lens or 2 for a 100× objective lens.
Adjust the focus again to ensure sharp images.
Acquire a two-channel image including H1-GFP and HP1α-cherry.
Select about 2 to 3 regions with 20 pixels in diameter (less than 2 μm) for bleaching.
Select 1 region of heterochromatin foci marked with HP1α or 1-2 non-foci regions.
Use a 488 nm Argon laser to bleach the H1-GFP signal.
Adjust the laser power and bleach time length to improve bleaching efficiency.
Ensure the bleaching efficiency is at least 70%.
Set the regions for bleaching on the image acquired.
Add a round region with both width and height set to 20 pixels.
Unfold the bleaching tool bar, and set “Start Bleaching after # scans” as 5 and “Repeat bleach after # scans” as 12.
Choose 488 nm laser for bleaching and adjust the laser power accordingly.
Click "Test Bleach" to determine the proper laser power or directly click “start experiment” to acquire a FRAP movie.
Set the cycles in the “Time Series” setting bar as 200 and interval as 1.0 s.
Open the “definite focus” setting bar, choose the “defined” model, and adjust settings to keep focus on the single channel image of H1-GFP.
Record an image series containing 5 frames before bleaching and at least 2–3 min time-lapse images after bleaching.
Replace cell culture medium before imaging work.
Settle the incubation system on the microscope at least 10 minutes before experiments.
Choose cells with proper H1-GFP signal level to avoid photobleaching.
Use ImageJ software to quantify fluorescence intensity from raw FRAP images acquired by confocal microscope.
Open raw images in Fiji ImageJ (Methods video S2).
Crop an interesting region containing one cell or only one nucleus.
Correct image shift and rotation using TurboReg and StackReg tool.
Select the appropriate tool: Image J > Plugins > StackReg.
Find bleached regions with the ROI manager tool.
Draw a circle of 20 pixels in diameter as specified for analysis.
Move the selecting circle to the bleached region at the fifth frame.
Click ‘update’ on the ROI manager tool window.
Add a circle at the non-nuclear region as background.
Measure the fluorescence intensity in the selected regions.
Open the Multi-measure tool through Plugins>Multi Measure.
Select all the circles and add them to the multi-measure box using the tool of add SP.
Click Multi-Measure on the tool window of the multi-measure plugin.
The intensity of the regions will be shown in a new window.
Copy the data and paste it into a new work sheet of excel.
Subtract the background intensity from the fluorescence intensity of FRAP regions.
Calculate the average fluorescence intensity in the test region with the first 5 frames.
Calculate the relative fluorescence intensity of regions after bleaching relative to the average fluorescence intensity of the same region before bleaching.
Combine all the relative fluorescence intensity data from heterochromatin regions in one group, and the data from euchromatin in another group.
Open GraphPad software.
Choose the “XY” model in graph construction.
Input the correct number of repeat value in “Y”.
Choose “Mean and Error” and “SEM” in the dialog.
Click “Create” to start.
Paste time points in the “X”.
Paste all relative fluorescence intensity data column by column.
Adjust setup of connecting line and error bar.
